newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end higher, 800 ceiling holds firm.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end higher, 800 ceiling holds firm.

text.p: Shares ended Monday's trading higher, led by active buying in blue chips, brokers said.
The composite index rose 12.12 points, or 1.54 percent, to a provisional close of 797.38. Trade volume totalled 23.1 million shares. Advancing shares beat decliners 590 to 240.
Despite the climb, the 800-point resistance line held firm.

"Although the climb was almost across the board, today's market energy was a bit scattered," said Samsung Securities broker Park Jae-young. "I expect some consolidation tomorrow, especially among blue chips."
Korea Electric Power (KEPCO) led Monday's trading, gaining 1,200 won to 28,600. It is seen as a target for overseas investors when the foreign shareholding ceiling is raised on October 1.
The limit for KEPCO and steelmaker POSCO will rise to 15 percent from 12 percent. All other companies will see their ceilings boosted to 20 percent from 18.
Chipmaker Samsung Electronics was another winner, climbing 1,700 won to 57,000 after falling to a low of 55,000 in early trade.
Several banks which are expected to see good earnings this year also gained.
Chungbuk Bank rose 50 won to 9,350. The Commercial Bank of Korea climbed 60 won to 7,610.
Brokers said Monday's rebound was due to institutional investors managing their portfolios ahead of the foreign ceiling rise.
